claimScope.reason: Standard68/69 gates, Standard69 preload-reserve floors, and candidate outputs were inspected during model construction; no lineage-disjoint final evidence set has been frozen.

evidenceBindings.measurementMeaning: Adult echocardiographic LV chamber volumes and systolic function.
evidenceBindings.limitations: Modality-, sex-, age-, and body-size-dependent reference context; it does not directly define this model's joint admissible interval.

evidenceBindings.measurementMeaning: Two-dimensional echocardiographic adult chamber-size reference ranges.
evidenceBindings.limitations: The cohort and measurement method do not identify a unique 0D-model parameter vector or a joint multivariate normal region.

evidenceBindings.measurementMeaning: CMR chamber-volume and function reference context across published cohorts.
evidenceBindings.limitations: The retained legacy evidence ID has a 2016 label but resolves to the 2015 publication; CMR and echocardiographic volumes are not interchangeable without a measurement model.

evidenceBindings.measurementMeaning: Adult three-dimensional echocardiographic RV volumes and ejection fraction.
evidenceBindings.limitations: A 0D chamber volume is compared only as broad construction context; acquisition and segmentation conventions remain different.

evidenceBindings.measurementMeaning: Resting forward cardiac output indexed to body surface area.
evidenceBindings.limitations: The model interval is an engineering synthesis across methods and cohorts, not a verbatim interval from either source.

evidenceBindings.measurementMeaning: Resting systemic forward stroke volume indexed to body surface area.
evidenceBindings.limitations: Stroke-volume index depends on heart rate, body-size convention, cohort, and acquisition method; the gate is a broad engineering envelope.

evidenceBindings.measurementMeaning: Right-heart echocardiographic assessment and healthy pulmonary arterial pressure context.
evidenceBindings.limitations: This does not directly support the exact 10-35 mmHg model interval or validate the current pulmonary waveform shape.

evidenceBindings.measurementMeaning: Supine resting pulmonary arterial wedge pressure in healthy subjects.
evidenceBindings.limitations: The retained legacy evidence ID uses the last author's name; the model reports mean LA pressure, not a simulated wedged-catheter measurement.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Whether the exact periodic classifier established the required period-one terminal state.
checkGroups.changeReason: Fail closed before interpreting any derived baseline measurement.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: Period-one settlement is numerical admissibility, not physiological normality or independent model validation.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: No clinical population interval applies to an exact periodic-classifier contract.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Algorithmic peak, variation, and central-range summaries of pressure during the associated semilunar-valve forward-flow episode.
checkGroups.changeReason: Reject obvious two-peak ringing and flat ejection plateaus observed during Standard65-to-68 construction.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: Pressure-peak prominence, total variation, central pressure range and peak phase depend on the trace resolution and the selected semilunar forward-flow episode; they do not measure a clinical ventricular pressure contour classification.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: No primary healthy-cohort distribution supports the exact peak-count, variation, central-range or peak-phase cutoffs. These remain construction choices made after observing earlier model artifacts.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Time-weighted mean and maximum raw LV-minus-Ao node pressure difference during native aortic forward flow.
checkGroups.changeReason: Constrain the non-stenotic baseline while retaining the model's explicit pressure-station limitation.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: This hydraulic node gradient is neither a Doppler Bernoulli gradient nor a simultaneous catheter LV-to-recovered-aortic pressure difference; pressure recovery and spatial acceleration are not observed.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: No matching healthy-population source establishes the exact mean or peak cutoffs for these model pressure stations. Stenosis diagnostic thresholds would not validate them.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Native AoV zero-flow opening to exact completed-beat closure; the observer requires agreement with the completed beat's accumulated positive-flow duration.
checkGroups.changeReason: Prevent a gradient reduction obtained by implausibly shortening or prolonging ejection.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: A single complete ejection episode is required. This hydraulic duration is shared with left ICT, IRT and Tei calculations, but is not color-TDI, Doppler-envelope or ECG timing; HR and population selection matter.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: The frozen construction interval is provisional. Similarity to the retrospective Copenhagen interval does not establish its historical derivation or cross-method validity.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: 1,969 Danish adults without cardiovascular disease or risk factors; median age 46 (IQR 33-58) years, 61.5% women, HR 63 +/- 10/min.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Color-TDI M-mode mitral-leaflet event timing; pooled 95% prediction intervals, not interchangeable with other Doppler or hydraulic event methods.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen interval is slightly broader at both endpoints; no observer-specific calibration has established equivalence.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Maximum and minimum accepted-step finite-difference derivative of absolute intracavitary LV pressure over the completed beat.
checkGroups.changeReason: Retain plausible contraction and relaxation rates while adjusting aortic ejection morphology.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: Accepted-step bandwidth, pressure loading, HR, preload, medication and catheter filtering affect extrema. Published negative dP/dt is often a positive magnitude, whereas this model stores a signed minimum; this is not a transmural derivative.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: The positive corridor overlaps small normal-LV patient series, but the frozen negative corridor excludes their resting means. Neither series supplies a population-normal acceptance interval; keep both corridors as warnings rather than validated pass/fail physiology.

sourceComparisons.locator: Abstract; resting values before ergometer exercise
sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: 13 patients described as having a normal LV; not a population-based, sex/age-stratified healthy sample.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Invasive maximal LV pressure rise and pressure-fall magnitude; the accessible abstract does not fully establish acquisition bandwidth.
sourceComparisons.sourceRange: Resting maximum +1721 +/- 378 mmHg/s; negative magnitude 1862 +/- 343 mmHg/s (mean +/- SD).
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The positive mean lies within the frozen corridor; the signed negative mean does not. Exercise values cannot justify a resting cutoff.

sourceComparisons.locator: Methods p. 757; normal-control table p. 759; abstract
sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: 18 normal controls including patients investigated for chest pain, murmurs or other indications; not a healthy population reference sample.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Millar LV micromanometer and continuous differentiator; average of five sinus beats, after premedication.
sourceComparisons.sourceRange: Maximum +1674 +/- 421 mmHg/s; negative magnitude 1864 +/- 390 mmHg/s (observed negative-magnitude range 1275-2772).
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The frozen relaxation corridor excludes the control mean and much of the observed range. Means/SDs and observed extrema are context, not newly selected cutoffs.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Ratio of peak native mitral forward volume flow in early and atrial filling windows anchored to the observed atrial-capture event.
checkGroups.changeReason: Provide a broad diastolic safety sentinel without claiming a clinical Doppler measurement.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: Volume-flow peaks are not leaflet-tip Doppler velocities; varying effective valve area can change their ratio. A complete post-capture inlet closure and identifiable E/A windows are required, and age, rhythm, HR and loading affect interpretation.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: The fixed corridor is provisional, not an age-specific Doppler normal interval. Better event anchoring does not remove the flow-versus-velocity observation mismatch.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Healthy reference data grouped by age; guideline echocardiographic assessment in adults, with age- and sex-aware supplementary data.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: PW Doppler mitral leaflet-tip E and A velocities, identified relative to ECG T and P waves; estimated fifth-to-95th percentiles.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen bounds truncate some healthy age-specific ranges and admit values outside others; numerical overlap cannot validate a native volume-flow ratio.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: ICT from exact MV closure to AoV zero-flow opening, IRT from exact AoV closure to MV zero-flow opening, and (ICT + IRT) divided by the matched aortic ejection duration.
checkGroups.changeReason: Detect compensation that improves one ejection output by distorting coupled systolic-diastolic timing.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: Closure landmarks and trace-interpolated openings must describe one complete beat. Tei is algebraically linked to ICT, IRT and the separately checked ejection time, so these are not independent constraints.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: The intervals remain provisional hydraulic timing targets. Matching some published endpoints does not establish a measurement-equivalence study or historical source derivation.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: 1,969 Danish adults without cardiovascular disease or risk factors; median age 46 (IQR 33-58) years, 61.5% women, HR 63 +/- 10/min.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Color-TDI M-mode mitral-leaflet event timing; pooled 95% prediction intervals, not interchangeable with other Doppler or hydraulic event methods.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: IRT and Tei endpoints match this pooled table, while the chosen ICT upper bound is wider. The source expressly limits generalization across measurement methods.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Completed-beat extrema of absolute Ao root-compliance-node pressure and time-weighted mean absolute RA pressure; the active AoP display uses this same Ao node.
checkGroups.changeReason: Maintain broad resting systemic-pressure compatibility as a construction safety envelope.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: The lumped central Ao node has no arterial propagation, peripheral amplification or pressure recovery and is not a brachial cuff observation. RA pressure is intracavitary, not transmural; its beat mean does not reproduce end-expiratory catheter averaging or IVC-based RAP estimation.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: No verified primary healthy central-aortic source establishes both chosen Ao ranges. The RA range is broader than the invasive reference below. All three are provisional resting construction targets.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Adult resting right-heart catheterization reference values summarized by the guideline, not a new sex-, age-, or BSA-stratified healthy cohort.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Supine catheter pressure, mid-thoracic zero and end-expiratory reading; output by direct Fick or thermodilution.
sourceComparisons.sourceRange: Mean RAP 2-6 mmHg; systemic systolic/diastolic pressure is illustrated as 120/80 mmHg, not a reference interval.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen RA corridor is wider. A single illustrative arterial pressure cannot substantiate either Ao endpoint.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Extrema of absolute model PA root-node pressure over the exact completed beat.
checkGroups.changeReason: Use broad resting pressure context as a sentinel while withholding a pulmonary-waveform validation claim.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: This is an invasive-like lumped pressure signal, not TR-derived RVSP/PASP or a spatially resolved catheter waveform; respiratory reference and averaging differ. RVSP is not PASP when an RV-to-PA gradient is present.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: The chosen systolic and diastolic upper bounds are broader than both cited invasive references. This remains a provisional pressure envelope, not confirmation of normal PAP or pulmonary waveform shape.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Adult resting right-heart catheterization reference values summarized by the guideline, not a new sex-, age-, or BSA-stratified healthy cohort.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Supine catheter pressure, mid-thoracic zero and end-expiratory reading; output by direct Fick or thermodilution.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen lower bounds match; the upper bounds are deliberately wider and are not the guideline's normal interval.

sourceComparisons.locator: Table 1; healthy resting supine catheterization data
sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: 47 studies, 1,187 healthy participants overall; resting supine systolic PAP available in 625, with heterogeneous age and sex representation.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Invasive resting supine PAP pooled across cohorts; mean +/- SD rather than a joint systolic/diastolic normal region.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: These distributions provide context but do not establish the chosen wider systolic and diastolic corridors.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Time-weighted completed-beat mean absolute LA pressure, exposed only as a labelled PCWP surrogate.
checkGroups.changeReason: Bound left-sided filling pressure while preserving the explicit station and measurement mismatch.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: Mean intracavitary LA pressure is not LVEDP, transmural LA pressure or an actual wedged-catheter observation. Wedge zero, respiratory sampling and transmission through the pulmonary circulation are not reproduced.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: The chosen upper limit has healthy PAWP context, but the lower bound lacks an exact source and no observation study establishes this model's LA-mean-to-PAWP equivalence.

sourceComparisons.locator: Main results; individual-data and zero-reference subgroup analyses
sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: 960 mainly nonobese healthy participants from 49 studies; individual-data subset n=159, median age 26 (IQR 23-53), 67% men.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Resting supine catheter PAWP, with heterogeneous zero references and respiratory conventions; significant sex differences.
sourceComparisons.sourceRange: Pooled PAWP 9.4 +/- 1.82 mmHg; upper limit 13 mmHg (mid-thoracic-zero subgroup 12.2 mmHg).
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen upper limit matches the pooled upper limit, not every subgroup. The study does not establish the chosen lower limit or validate mean model LA pressure as a wedge observation.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Valve-event-defined 0D LV volumes indexed to the reference BSA and their event-defined ejection fraction.
checkGroups.changeReason: Create a deliberately broad cross-modality construction corridor rather than a joint population-normal claim.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: ED/ES are volumes at native inlet/outlet closure, not necessarily global extrema. Event definitions can align with imaging, but 0D cavity boundaries lack echo/CMR segmentation conventions. Fixed reference BSA does not select a sex/age cohort; EF is derived from the two volumes.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: The frozen corridor combines context across methods; its volume endpoints do not reproduce the cited echo or CMR intervals, and its independent marginal gates are not a joint healthy distribution.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Adult sex-specific echocardiographic reference data.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: 2D biplane LV volumes indexed to BSA; ED/ES may use valve events or cavity extrema; normal ranges based on mean +/- 2 SD.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: Chosen EF is the sex-union; the volume corridor is not the sex-union and admits larger volumes.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: 734 healthy adults (320 men, 414 women), age 45.8 +/- 13.3 years, predominantly white Europeans from 22 institutions.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Biplane Simpson 2D echo, excluding papillary muscles and trabeculae from the cavity; BSA indexing does not remove age/sex effects.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen volume and EF bounds are broader than these sex-specific intervals; the source does not support their exact endpoints.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Pooled adult European cohorts, ages 20-80 years; sex-specific results.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: 1.5 T SSFP CMR with LV papillary muscles included in mass; mean +/- 2 SD.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen corridor is not a CMR normal interval and can exclude source-normal EDVi or EF while admitting much lower volumes.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Valve-event-defined 0D RV volumes indexed to the reference BSA and their event-defined ejection fraction.
checkGroups.changeReason: Retain broad RV size/function safety bounds without extending the current systemic and left-heart claim.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: Native TV/PV closure volumes and derived EF do not specify a 3D-echo or CMR segmentation method. BSA indexing alone does not remove sex/age effects; EF and the two event volumes are algebraically linked.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: The volume bounds match a union of male/female 3D-echo ranges, not a population-specific or cross-modality range. The EF endpoints combine age/sex subgroup extremes rather than defining a single healthy cohort.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Adult sex-specific 3D-echo data; supplemental RV EF limits further stratified by age.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: 3D-echo RV volume segmentation and BSA indexing; subgroup EF limits are fifth/95th percentiles.
sourceComparisons.sourceRange: Men: EDVi 35-87, ESVi 10-44 mL/m2; women: 32-74, 8-36. Subgroup EF extremes include 42% and 82%; general RV EF below 45% is abnormal.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: Volume bounds reproduce the sex-union. EF bounds span subgroup extremes, not a universal normal range.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Healthy adult cohorts aged 20-68 years, sex-specific results; indexed RV ESV uses the Hudsmith cohort.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: 1.5 T SSFP CMR with RV trabeculations and papillary muscles in the cavity; mean +/- 2 SD.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: Chosen volume bounds exclude substantial CMR-normal values; the 3D-echo corridor cannot be called a broad cross-modality RV normal interval.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Positive-only native AoV flow integrated for stroke volume and converted to cardiac output over the completed beat, both indexed to reference BSA.
checkGroups.changeReason: Maintain broad resting forward-flow compatibility across the admitted HR values.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: Forward volume is not signed net aortic flow or EDV-minus-ESV when regurgitation or other routes exist. CI and SVI are linked by HR, so at a fixed HR they are not independent targets; reference BSA and body habitus remain relevant.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: CI has an exact guideline interval, but SVI is a cross-source construction choice. The retained Barratt-Boyes binding was metadata-verified only and does not provide a verified quantitative derivation here.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Adult resting right-heart catheterization reference values summarized by the guideline, not a new sex-, age-, or BSA-stratified healthy cohort.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Supine catheter pressure, mid-thoracic zero and end-expiratory reading; output by direct Fick or thermodilution.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: CI endpoints match exactly; SVI endpoints do not. Fick/thermodilution output is not necessarily the model's positive-only valve-flow output.

sourceComparisons.locator: Methods; healthy-group results and age analysis
sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: 144 healthy nonathletic adults, 68 women, ages 21-81 (mean 39 +/- 16) years; BMI <=30, no cardiovascular disease or medication.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Supine free-breathing ascending-aortic phase-contrast CMR; signed whole-cycle flow integrated for SV, Mosteller BSA.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen SVI interval is close to, but not identical to, a calculated mean +/- 2 SD interval of 37-65. Such a calculation is not a published universal normal cutoff.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Time-weighted mean and maximum raw RV-minus-PA node pressure difference while native PV flow is positive over the completed beat.
checkGroups.changeReason: Record the existing Standard70 right-heart gradient sentinels without promoting them to left-objective groups or changing their numerical limits.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: The model's hydraulic gradient is not a Doppler Bernoulli or recovered catheter gradient; an explicit outlet node does not provide spatial velocity, pressure recovery or an invasive sensor model.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: No source establishes the exact mean and peak healthy cutoffs for these pressure stations. These remain non-stenotic construction guards, not clinical normal-gradient intervals.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Native PV zero-flow opening to exact completed-beat closure; the observer requires agreement with the completed beat's accumulated positive-flow duration.
checkGroups.changeReason: Record the existing Standard70 pulmonary ejection-time corridor with its missing method-matched normative evidence.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: A complete single ejection episode is required. This duration also enters right ICT, IRT and Tei calculations; hydraulic timing is not a Doppler-envelope or tissue-Doppler measurement and depends on HR/loading.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: No exact primary normal interval was identified for this observer and target population. Retain the frozen interval only as a provisional physiological target; left-sided LVET data do not establish a right-sided range.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Maximum and minimum accepted-step finite-difference derivative of absolute intracavitary RV pressure over the completed beat.
checkGroups.changeReason: Reclassify the existing Standard70 RV derivative corridors as reference warnings without altering the recorded numerical bounds.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: These load- and bandwidth-dependent extrema are neither transmural pressure derivatives nor the mean RV-to-RA pressure-gradient rise inferred over a selected TR velocity interval. Signed negative extrema must not be confused with published pressure-fall magnitudes.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: No verified source establishes either frozen normal corridor. Sparse normal-PAP invasive data and a method-specific abnormal Doppler threshold justify contextual warnings, not hard healthy-population acceptance limits.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Adult right-heart echocardiography; normal-reference data are limited.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: TR Doppler 1-to-2 m/s upslope converted to a 12 mmHg pressure-gradient rise divided by time.
sourceComparisons.sourceRange: RV dP/dt below 400 mmHg/s is abnormal for this Doppler method.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: This is not the maximum native intracavitary derivative and does not establish either chosen endpoint or a normal upper limit.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: 34 patients: eight with normal PAP, 17 with pulmonary hypertension, nine with pulmonary hypertension and RV failure; not a general healthy reference cohort.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Maximal invasive RV pressure-fall magnitude; strong pressure-load dependence, with acquisition detail incompletely resolved by the abstract.
sourceComparisons.sourceRange: Normal-PAP group 170 +/- 20 mmHg/s; pulmonary-hypertension groups 670 +/- 60 mmHg/s, with or without RV failure.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: Both loading groups can fit the broad signed negative corridor. The reported summary values are not a healthy reference interval and cannot define its bounds.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Ratio of peak native tricuspid forward volume flow in early and atrial filling windows anchored to the observed atrial-capture event.
checkGroups.changeReason: Record the existing Standard70 inflow-ratio corridor without claiming a clinical Doppler measurement.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: Requires identifiable windows and an observed post-capture inlet closure. Volume-flow peaks do not equal Doppler velocities if effective valve area changes; respiration, HR, rhythm, age and loading remain relevant.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: The numerical corridor resembles a guideline Doppler interval but remains provisional for the native-flow observer; the source upper endpoint is exclusive whereas the frozen gate is inclusive.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Adult echocardiographic reference context.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: PW tricuspid inflow E/A velocities; end-expiratory averaging over at least five beats.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen numeric endpoints match, but flow-versus-velocity and respiratory averaging differ; this is not method-matched validation.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: ICT from exact TV closure to PV zero-flow opening, IRT from exact PV closure to TV zero-flow opening, and (ICT + IRT) divided by the matched pulmonary ejection duration.
checkGroups.changeReason: Record the existing Standard70 event-timing corridors while retaining their construction origin and observation mismatch.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: One complete valve-event sequence is required. Tei is algebraically linked to ICT, IRT and the separately checked pulmonary ET; PW-Doppler, TDI and hydraulic timings are different observations.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: No primary source was identified for the chosen joint ICT/IRT/Tei corridors. The source below supplies method-specific context, not equivalent normal intervals; all three remain provisional physiological targets.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Adult right-heart echocardiography.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: PW-Doppler or tissue-Doppler MPI and tissue-Doppler IVRT, not native valve-flow events.
sourceComparisons.sourceRange: MPI <0.40 by PW Doppler or <0.55 by TDI; IVRT <=73 ms by TDI.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: The chosen upper IRT and Tei bounds are wider, and no chosen lower bound or ICT interval follows from these thresholds.

checkGroups.measurementMeaning: Algorithmic full-cycle PA pressure peak count, thresholded PV forward-episode count, primary-episode PV flow peak count and maximal post-episode PA rebound.
checkGroups.changeReason: Record Standard70 pulmonary ringing and re-ejection guards as construction-only waveform criteria.
checkGroups.observationLimitations: The episode threshold and peak-prominence algorithm define these observations; the post-episode rebound is not an invasive dicrotic-notch metric. One peak does not characterize the entire pressure or flow contour.
checkGroups.evidenceGap: No primary normal distribution supports the exact one-peak, one-episode or rebound cutoffs. A qualitative Doppler flow shape must not be cited as proof of these pressure-waveform thresholds.

sourceComparisons.targetPopulation: Adult resting right-heart echocardiography.
sourceComparisons.observationMeaning: Qualitative RVOT Doppler velocity waveform: parabolic with a midsystolic peak.
sourceComparisons.comparisonToChosenBounds: Qualitative flow context only; it establishes no peak-prominence, PAP peak-count or post-PV-closure rebound cutoff.

policyRevisions.changeReason: Capture the current Standard68 mint policy and healthy-reference context after retrospective provenance repair.

preloadReservePolicyRevisions.changeReason: Freeze the Standard69-specific relative CO, pressure-flow slope, and relative EDV floors after exploratory candidate inspection. These are construction-only non-regression thresholds, not independently validated physiological cutoffs.
